criteria.name: reusability
criteria.description: Can the module be used in different projects without modification?

criteria.name: generalApplicability
criteria.description: How broadly applicable is this module across different domains?

criteria.name: codeQuality
criteria.description: Is the code well-structured, typed, and follows best practices?

criteria.name: documentationPotential
criteria.description: Can the module be easily documented for public use?

criteria.name: maintenanceBurden
criteria.description: How much ongoing maintenance will be required? (5 = low burden, 1 = high burden)

criteria.name: securitySensitivity
criteria.description: Does the module handle sensitive data or have security implications? (5 = not sensitive, 1 = highly sensitive)

candidates.description: Circuit Breaker pattern implementation for API resilience. Provides fault tolerance for external service calls.
candidates.notes: Classic design pattern implementation. Self-contained with no external dependencies beyond TypeScript. Highly valuable for any project making external API calls.

candidates.description: Accessibility utilities and ARIA helpers for building accessible React/Next.js applications.
candidates.notes: Accessibility is a critical concern for web development. These utilities can help developers build WCAG-compliant applications more easily.

candidates.description: Seeded Random Number Generator implementation for deterministic random sequences. Useful for games, simulations, and testing.

securityConcerns.description: This is NOT a cryptographic random number generator. Should not be used for security-sensitive operations like token generation or encryption keys.

candidates.notes: Seeded RNG is valuable for reproducible game states, procedural generation, and deterministic testing. Must clearly document that it's not cryptographically secure.

candidates.description: JSON-LD structured data generation utilities for SEO. Helps generate schema.org markup for better search engine visibility.
candidates.notes: SEO is important for public-facing websites. JSON-LD utilities can help developers implement structured data without deep knowledge of schema.org specifications.

candidates.description: Complete turn-based game engine with items, maps, ballistics, enemies, encounters, recipes, and skills systems.
candidates.notes: Complex game engine with multiple interconnected systems. While valuable, the extraction effort is high and maintenance burden significant. Consider extracting individual systems (RNG, ballistics) separately first.

candidates.description: Game-specific React components including StashGrid, RaidView, WeaponModdingPanel, and other game UI elements.
candidates.notes: Coupled with the game engine. Best released as a companion package after the game engine is extracted. UI components are well-structured but domain-specific.

candidates.description: WhatsApp Web.js integration for sending and receiving WhatsApp messages in Next.js applications.

securityConcerns.description: WhatsApp Web.js uses an unofficial API. Meta may block or restrict access at any time. Not suitable for production-critical applications.
Handles message content which could contain sensitive user data. Requires careful data handling documentation.

candidates.notes: Useful for prototyping and internal tools. Should clearly document the unofficial nature of the API and associated risks. May require significant maintenance as whatsapp-web.js evolves.

candidates.description: Sleep analysis logic for processing and interpreting sleep data patterns.

securityConcerns.description: Handles health-related data which may be subject to HIPAA or other health data regulations depending on use case.

candidates.notes: Niche but potentially valuable for health-tech applications. Consider combining with other health analysis utilities if more modules are discovered.

candidates.description: Three.js/React Three Fiber components including EnergyWaves, Eye, HeroCanvas and other 3D visual effects for portfolio/landing pages.
candidates.notes: Visually impressive 3D components for portfolio sites. Note: GSAP has a commercial license for certain uses - may need to make it an optional peer dependency or provide alternatives.

strongCandidates: circuitBreaker (score: 87) - Classic pattern, low extraction effort, no dependencies
accessibility (score: 82) - High value for web developers, React-focused
rng (score: 79) - Simple, self-contained, useful for games/simulations
goodCandidates: gameEngine (score: 57) - Complex but valuable, high extraction effort
whatsapp (score: 56) - Useful but unofficial API risks

monorepoRecommendation.rationale: All candidates are Next.js/React focused and share a common scope (@opensourceframework). Using the existing monorepo structure provides: unified tooling (Turborepo, changesets), consistent CI/CD, shared development standards, and easier cross-package testing. The packages are small enough that repository size is not a concern.
monorepoRecommendation.alternativeConsidered: Polyrepo would only make sense for the game engine if it grows significantly or requires different maintainership in the future.
